# 4 Benchmarks (continued)

## BLENDED BENCHMARKS (OR BALANCED BENCHMARKS) {#a}

Blended benchmarks are a specific type of customised benchmark, consisting of a blend of multiple indexes, typically from different index providers and representing a range of asset classes, potentially using a range of methodologies. Blended benchmarks are most commonly used in conjunction with balanced investment strategies or policy benchmarks for asset owners.

### Fixed-weight and dynamised benchmarks {#b}

Blended benchmarks are often defined using fixed weights for certain asset categories. The performance of assets categories will diverge over time, thus impacting the original strategic asset allocation. It is essential that the frequency of fixed-weight rebalancing is established. within the benchmark definition. If the initial fixed weight is allowed to float with the performance of the individual categories, the impact compared to a genuine fixed weight can be significant, as demonstrated in Table 4.7.

Exhibit 4.3 illustrates how the floating weights are calculated for each quarter or, in other words, dynamised. The quarterly balanced fixed-weight index outperforms the floating-weight index. This outperformance is for the most part generated in the third quarter; the fixed-weight index is required to reduce the exposure to equities at the beginning of the period immediately before a big fall in the market. Note that to replicate the annual return resulting from applying the 50%:50% fixed weight to the category annual returns, floating weights must be used each quarter.

**Table 4.7 — Fixed-weight and dynamised benchmarks**

| | First quarter | | Second quarter | | Third quarter | | Fourth quarter | | Year |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | Weight | Return | Weight | Return | Weight | Return | Weight | Return | Return |
| *Fixed weights* | | | | | | | | | |
| Equities | 50% | 10.4 | 50% | 3.5 | 50% | −15.7 | 50% | 12.7 | **8.56** |
| Bonds | 50% | 2.3 | 50% | 1.3 | 50% | 1.4 | 50% | 8.7 | **14.22** |
| **Total** | | **6.35** | | **2.4** | | **−7.15** | | **10.70** | **11.94** |
| *Floating weights* | | | | | | | | | |
| Equities | 50% | 10.4 | 51.90% | 3.5 | 52.44% | −15.7 | 47.83% | 12.7 | **8.56** |
| Bonds | 50% | 2.3 | 48.10% | 1.3 | 47.56% | 1.4 | 52.17% | 8.7 | **14.22** |
| **Total** | | **6.35** | | **2.44** | | **−7.57** | | **10.61** | **11.39** |

### Exhibit 4.3 — Dynamised benchmark {#c}

Applying the 50%:50% weight to the annual returns the total benchmark return is:

$$50\% \times 8.56 + 50\% \times 14.22 = 11.39$$

To achieve this return using quarterly data we need to reweight each quarter to reflect underlying market movements:

Second-quarter weights

$$50\% \times 10.4\% = 55.2\% \qquad 50\% \times 2.3\% = 51.15\% \qquad \text{Total } 106.35\%$$

Revised weights

$$\frac{55.2\%}{106.35\%} = 51.9\% \qquad \frac{51.15\%}{106.35\%} = 48.1\%$$

Third-quarter weights

$$51.9\% \times 3.5\% = 53.72\% \qquad 48.1\% \times 1.3\% = 48.72\% \qquad \text{Total } 102.44\%$$

Revised weights

$$\frac{53.72\%}{102.44\%} = 52.44\% \qquad \frac{48.72\%}{102.44\%} = 47.56\%$$

Fourth-quarter weights

$$52.44\% \times {-15.7\%} = 44.21\% \qquad 47.56\% \times 1.4\% = 48.23\% \qquad \text{Total } 92.43\%$$

Revised weights

$$\frac{44.21\%}{92.43\%} = 47.83\% \qquad \frac{48.72\%}{92.43\%} = 52.17\%$$

With the revised weights the quarterly benchmark returns compound to 11.39%; using fixed weights the benchmark return compounds to 11.94%, a significant difference.
